events.title: The politics of pink: how Iran uses cuteness to rebrand violence
events.summary: Pink missiles, pink drones and pink firearms. Women with uncovered hair—braids, ponytails, short bobs—stood beside weapons, waved flags and smiled for cameras in scenes broadcast across Iranian media. Tehran appears willing to try almost anything to preserve power.

events.title: Bread shortages, soaring prices strain households in Iran, residents say
events.summary: Bread shortages and steep price hikes are undermining access to a key staple for many in Iran, with citizen accounts received by Iran International describing long lines, flour shortages and prices far exceeding official rates.

events.title: Iran says no decision yet on talks as Pakistan prepares to host US team
events.summary: Iran said on Monday it had not yet decided whether to join a second round of talks with the United States, even as Pakistan prepared to host a US delegation, with Tehran accusing Washington of violating the ceasefire and showing no real seriousness about diplomacy.

events.title: War-hit homeowners feel abandoned as Iran’s reconstruction aid fades
events.summary: The Iranian government has stepped back from earlier promises to compensate homeowners whose properties were destroyed in US-Israeli strikes, triggering anger among residents who expected the state to take responsibility for rebuilding.

events.title: 100 days on: the anatomy of Iran’s January crackdown
events.summary: One hundred days after protests erupted across Iran in January 2026, the events still stand out as one of the most widespread and violent protest waves the country has seen in recent years.

events.title: 100 days on: why Iran’s January protests spread across social classes
events.summary: One hundred days after protests erupted across Iran in January 2026, the events continue to reveal something fundamental about Iranian society: many people now fear silence more than they fear protest.
